replies.author: @JamesPhieffer
replies.text:
​@HiddenCanada I don't think there was. We were mostly sampling. Set gill nets (illegal except for the MNR) at regular points, then collect them, and log their measurements, stomach content, sex, etc, along with removing their otolith (ear bone) which charts growth with rings, same as a tree.

replies.text: ​@HiddenCanada  yes. I'm familiar with that plus a more recent masters thesis from Queen's. Forgive my seeming arrogance but they got it wrong. replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: The plunge-pool explanation was one of the theories investigated. The 1960s drilling helped distinguish between them, and the researchers concluded the basin was a limestone sinkhole. That’s why the video follows that explanation.

comments.text: My mother was born on Lake on the Mountain, so called because the Glendora ferry was lower than the lake.
